question.text: Meera invests Rs. 2,00,000 in a fixed deposit paying 7.5% interest compounded annually. The approximate maturity value after 6 years is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook gives FV = PV × (1+r)^n. Here FV = 2,00,000 × (1.075)^6 = 2,00,000 × 1.54330 ≈ Rs. 3,08,660. The Trap: Rs. 2,90,000 is the simple interest result (2,00,000 + 2,00,000 × 7.5% × 6 = 2,90,000) — it ignores compounding entirely. Note: Always use the compound-interest formula for annually-compounded FDs; minor rounding in the (1.075)^6 factor moves the answer by only a few hundred rupees.
